Modernization is a behavior change wearing a container costume

Modernization is not 'lift and shift' (which moves your problems and adds a bill) or 'rewrite everything' (which never ships). It is wave-based refactoring: containerize, externalize state, adopt managed services where they remove undifferentiated work, and retire VMs on evidence — one workload class at a time.

The discipline mirrors the data domain's strangler pattern: dual-run where risk demands it, diff-driven cutover, and retirement gates that require the workload to prove its reliability posture on the new runtime first.
Below: the failure modes that strand modernization halfway, the reference architecture of the strangler waves, and the console that tracks the estate's retirement honestly.
Four failure modes that strand modernization halfway
Each of these produces 'we are containerized' estates that still behave like VMs — the countermeasures make resilience and observability gates, not aspirations.

widgets.title: Modernization waves — click each for scope and unblocked metric

stages.name: Wave 1 — Edge seams
stages.detail: The two modules with divergent change velocity extract first: customer notifications and document generation. Low blast radius, immediate deploy-frequency win, team learns the ratchet mechanics on forgiving ground.

stages.name: Wave 2 — Pricing core
stages.detail: Pricing extracts with its schema owned outright; the anti-corruption layer translates legacy discount codes. Business unblocks dynamic pricing the monolith could not ship.

stages.name: Wave 3 — Customer 360
stages.detail: The tangled data module: state transfer via event stream first, service extraction second. This is the wave the plan reserves the most rehearsal for.

stages.name: Wave 4 — Ledger & audit
stages.detail: The financial core moves last, when extraction mechanics are boring. Immutable event log lands with it — the audit story improves as a side effect.

widgets.note: Waves are sequenced by risk × learning value, not by module size — the edge seams exist to make the ratchet boring before the pricing core needs it.

widgets.title: Target architecture — click nodes for the seam contract

nodes.label: Web & mobile
nodes.detail: Channels talk only to the API gateway; no channel reaches into services or the core directly — the rule that keeps seams honest.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.detail: Routing with per-service auth and rate budgets; the ratchet lives here — traffic shifts are gateway config, not code.

nodes.label: Pricing service
nodes.detail: Owns its schema outright; the ACL translates legacy discount semantics until the core stops being asked.

nodes.label: Customer 360
nodes.detail: Event-carried state from the legacy core; read models per channel need.

nodes.label: Ledger service
nodes.detail: Immutable event log with reconciliation against the core during the transition window.

nodes.label: Legacy core
nodes.detail: Shrinks by design: each wave moves call volume out; the remainder is measured weekly and reported without euphemism.

nodes.label: Event backbone
nodes.detail: Replayable topics between services and core — the integration fabric from the hyperautomation practice.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read the seam contracts. The gateway is where the strangler actually strangles — everything else is consequence.
